solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Can awkward PROs in meeting stop employment?

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of place, so the letters beside it are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written
ho! is an old call to halt
use is employment of something

explanation.surface: A question whether clumsy public-relations people at a meeting might put an end to someone's job.
explanation.walkthrough: Can is slang for prison, which looks like a verb in the surface. Meeting just joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for a jail, and a prison house is literally a building used as a jail.

clue.text: A failing model set apart — roughcast for Americans

parts.note: this article is the letter dropped from the phrase that follows

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a fresh form
the article is said to be failing, that is, missing from the following phrase

parts.note: the letters taken as written, with one A then removed
the printed punctuation mark is called a dash

explanation.surface: A failed model has been kept apart from others, with an odd note about American building plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark in the middle of the clue is itself wordplay: its name supplies the last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives spatterdash as an American term for roughcast, a coarse plaster finish for outside walls.

clue.text: Second domain one's ignored always

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: an empire is a domain ruled over
one is I, the Roman numeral; this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone's second territory is always neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: One's ignored means the I goes missing from the domain word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sempre is the Italian musical direction meaning throughout, used in English scores for always.

clue.text: Cut around hydrant in lighthouse

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps about the next piece

parts.note: to pare is to cut thinly
H is the map and street-sign abbreviation for hydrant

explanation.surface: Someone trims round a fire hydrant inside a lighthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hydrant appears on British street plates marking fire hydrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Phare is an old word, from French, for a lighthouse or beacon tower.

clue.text: Vote for navy in censure? Could be a duty

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one thing is swapped in where the other stood

parts.note: a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper
RN is the Royal Navy, the letters taken out
tarnation, a mild form of damnation, is used in Chambers for censure

explanation.surface: A question whether a vote for the navy might count as a reprimand; then the idea it might be an obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: Put X in place of the RN inside the censure word. The definition is a feature of the answer: a duty is one example of a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty, such as customs or excise, is one kind of levy, so it is an instance of taxation.

clue.text: Conduct around child about right

indicators.note: about means the young one's word goes around the other letter

parts.note: a tot is a small child
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone shows a child round, with a remark about what is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes two words: to trot someone around is to lead them round on a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers allows trot as a verb meaning to lead or escort someone about, as in trotting a visitor round.

clue.text: Line about Hungary's let in

indicators.note: about means the lining word goes round the country letter

parts.note: to encase is to enclose or line something
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: A railway line around Hungary has been allowed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchase is to set a jewel into a surround, which Chambers glosses as to let in or insert.

clue.text: Little monster disappeared inside, damn!

indicators.note: inside means that word sits within the exclamation

parts.note: drat is a mild curse like damn
gone means disappeared

explanation.surface: Someone curses because a naughty child has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: Little monster suggests a badly behaved child, but here it is a literal small dragon.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonet is a young or small dragon, so it is a diminutive monster.

clue.text: Nationalist supporting display in Glasgow club

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed underneath, so the first-named letter goes after the other piece

parts.note: to air is to display or show
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: A Nationalist backs a show put on at a Glasgow club.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, supporting means placed underneath, so N comes after the display word. Airn is Scots for iron, and a golf iron is a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Airn is the Scots form of iron, and an iron is a kind of golf club, so a Glaswegian would call it one.

clue.text: Hot German bread, only one left

indicators.note: only one left means a doubled letter is reduced to a single copy

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: Fresh, warm German bread, with only one loaf remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot looks like oven-fresh, but it is slang for stolen goods. The bread has two Ls; one is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, as with goods too recently taken to sell safely.

clue.text: Girl out of practice to try again

indicators.note: out of means the name is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a rehearsal is a practice
Sal is a short girl's name, here the letters removed

explanation.surface: A girl leaves rehearsal so she can attempt something again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehear a case is to hear it again in court, that is, to try it again.

clue.text: Gastropods could be swimming near it

indicators.note: swimming letters move about, so they may settle in another order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Snails might be paddling close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerita is a genus of sea snails, so its members are gastropods; the singular genus name stands for the group.

clue.text: A call-girl dancing with pole regularly is fabulous (perhaps)

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, ending up in a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word before it

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A prostitute pole-dancing is said to be legendary.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means of the nature of a fable, not marvellous; the (perhaps) admits a fable is only one kind of allegory.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a story with a moral meaning beneath the surface, which is what allegorical writing is.

clue.text: Hastings, for example getting behind independent cinema

indicators.note: getting behind means coming after, so the named piece follows the single letter

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
Max Hastings is a British journalist and historian, an example of a Max

explanation.surface: Someone from Hastings backs an independent picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings looks like the town on the south coast of England, but it is the surname of the writer Sir Max Hastings. Getting behind puts his first name after I.
explanation.definitionFit: IMAX is a large-screen film format, and an IMAX is a cinema that shows it.

clue.text: Bird song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bird is British slang for a girl, and this is a girl's name
second meaning: a joyful song, especially at Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests birdsong; in British slang a bird is a young woman, so the first meaning is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a common female name, fitting the slang sense of bird, and a carol is a festive hymn.

clue.text: Chap from Devon pares dodgy article

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written
the definite article

explanation.surface: A man from Devon trims down a suspect item.
explanation.walkthrough: Chap looks like a noun for a man, but it is a verb: to crack, as skin does in cold weather. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreathe is a Devon dialect verb meaning to chap or roughen, as skin does in cold wind.

clue.text: Part of fruit some stewed with beef

indicators.note: stewed means cooked down and stirred, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters taken as written
to beef or carp is to complain

explanation.surface: A kitchen picture: some fruit stewed together with beef.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like meat for the stew, but it is the verb meaning to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The mesocarp is the middle layer of a fruit's wall, the fleshy part between skin and stone.

clue.text: One's no longer inside a part in Peru

indicators.note: in means the role phrase sits within the country's code

parts.note: PE is the international code for Peru
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: An actor is no longer cast, having taken a part in Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside is slang for in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A parolee is a prisoner released early on conditions, someone who is no longer behind bars.

clue.text: Critic on the Spectator?

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a spectator is a viewer

explanation.surface: Someone who writes reviews for The Spectator, the British weekly magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a British political weekly, so the surface suggests a journalist there; split it, and on and Spectator give the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer assesses books, plays or films in print, which is the job of a critic.

clue.text: Broods about leader in Express on worms

indicators.note: about means the broods word wraps around what follows

parts.note: a nid or nide is a brood of pheasants

indicators.note: 'leader in' keeps only the first letter of 'Express'

parts.note: the first letter of Express
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone frets about the editorial in the Express newspaper on the subject of worms.
explanation.walkthrough: Broods looks like a verb for brooding, but it is a plural noun for pheasant families.
explanation.definitionFit: Nereids are marine bristle worms, the ragworm family, named after the sea nymphs.

clue.text: Rascal gets a dram for short time in boozer

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: a tinker is a mischievous child or rascal
dr is the abbreviation for dram
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A scamp downs a quick dram in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer is British slang for a pub, but here it means the person who drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is a heavy drinker, a person who takes a lot of alcohol.

clue.text: Kiwi fool available to order in New Guinea, initially

indicators.note: in means the availability word sits inside the pair of initials
initially means taking the first letter of each of those words

parts.note: first letters of New and Guinea
on is available, as a dish on the menu

explanation.surface: A silly New Zealander can be had to order in New Guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi looks like the fruit or bird, but means a New Zealander.
explanation.definitionFit: Nong is Australian and New Zealand slang for an idiot.

clue.text: Man's ringing second-class soccer club

indicators.note: ringing means circling, so the possessive goes around the grade letter

parts.note: his means belonging to a man
B is the second grade

explanation.surface: A man phones a lower-league football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringing looks like phoning, but means encircling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibs is the nickname of Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club.

clue.text: Doctor to media, millions giving up salt

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered in order
giving up means abandoning, so that letter leaves the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for millions; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A medic speaks to the press, millions losing their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a medic, but is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodate is a chemical salt of iodic acid.

clue.text: Run before very much outmoded backhanded stroke

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for run in cricket
ever so means very much

explanation.surface: Someone sprints before a very old-fashioned backhand shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Outmoded belongs to the definition: the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverso is an obsolete fencing term for a backhanded blow, a cut delivered from the reverse side.

clue.text: Temper tantrum abroad is shown up in protests

indicators.note: in a down answer, shown up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: snit is American for a fit of temper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign temper tantrum is shown off during demonstrations.
explanation.walkthrough: Abroad signals an American word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ins are protests where people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: A pair in Goa treated reproductive organs of seaweed

parts.note: in cricket a pair is two noughts, out for nothing in both innings

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple in Goa in India receive care for their reproductive organs.
explanation.walkthrough: A pair is a cricket term: scoring zero in both innings, so two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oogonia are the female sex organs of certain algae and fungi, where eggs form.

clue.text: Old Glaswegian messenger about to stop working

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: An elderly messenger in Glasgow is about to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Glaswegian marks an archaic Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadie was a Scottish errand-boy or messenger, the same word as golf's caddie.

clue.text: Original matter imperfectly taken up after leaving LA

indicators.note: in a down answer, taken up means written from bottom to top
after leaving means once those letters have departed from the word

parts.note: lamely means imperfectly, not convincingly
these two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Original material poorly picked up after departing Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like Los Angeles but is just two letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Ylem is the primordial substance from which the elements were supposedly formed in the Big Bang.

clue.text: Scots born before 1603 against drinking neat rum

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the first word holds the others

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: rum is British slang for odd, so the letters are made strange in order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Old Scots opposed to drinking undiluted rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink, but is an adjective meaning odd. 1603 is the union of the Scottish and English crowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenati were those born before a set date, in Scotland before the union of crowns in 1603.

clue.text: Bracken down under pitch area

parts.note: tar is pitch
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Australian bracken growing on a pitch area.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like a sports ground, but means tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tara is the New Zealand and Australian name for bracken fern.

clue.text: Diverse mixture in Germany sadly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the pair is written backwards

parts.note: D is the international code for Germany
alas expresses sadness

explanation.surface: A mixed bag in Germany has unfortunately been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad can mean any confused or varied mixture, as in word salad.

clue.text: Lyric's tuneful but one Spice Girl's walked out

indicators.note: walked out means left, so that name is removed

parts.note: melodic means tuneful
Mel B and Mel C were Spice Girls; the name is removed

explanation.surface: A song is melodious, though a Spice Girl has left the band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a British pop group with two members called Mel.
explanation.definitionFit: Odic means of the nature of an ode, and a lyric poem is often an ode, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Seemingly endless once, try largest Canary Island if running

indicators.note: to try something is to test it out, so the letters are put through a new order
running means running off, so the conditional word leaves the name

parts.note: Tenerife is the biggest of the Canary Islands
these letters are removed

explanation.surface: An attempt at a holiday on Tenerife if travelling, which seems never to end.
explanation.walkthrough: Once marks the word as archaic; seemingly endless is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eterne is an old poetic form of eternal, meaning without end.

clue.text: A river recalled in Canadian capital

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the Niger is a West African river

explanation.surface: A river remembered in a Canadian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the capital city of the Canadian province of Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Work or spare time for office employees

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between work or leisure for clerical staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporaries are temps, staff hired for short periods to fill office jobs.
